name: Wages and Compensation
text: The Employer shall pay the Employee a gross annual cost-to-company of such amount as specified in Annexure A ('CTC'), inclusive of all statutory contributions. The salary shall be disbursed monthly on or before the seventh (7th) day of the following month, in accordance with Section 17 of the Code on Wages, 2019. The compensation structure shall comprise: (a) Basic Salary (not less than fifty percent of the gross salary); (b) House Rent Allowance; (c) Special Allowance; and (d) such other components as specified in Annexure A. The Employer shall deduct Tax Deducted at Source ('TDS') in accordance with the Income Tax Act, 1961, and shall issue Form 16 annually. Any revision to the Employee's compensation shall be communicated in writing. The Employer shall ensure that the total compensation is not less than the applicable minimum rate of wages prescribed under Section 5 of the Code on Wages, 2019 for the relevant category of employment.

legal_basis.note: Definition of wages — excluded allowances above one-half of total remuneration are added back
Payment of not less than the minimum rate of wages
Time limit for payment of wages
No deductions except those authorised under the Code
TDS on salary. Not affected by the labour Codes.

invalid_if: Salary below applicable minimum wage under Minimum Wages Act 1948

authoring_note: LABOUR CODES, 21 NOVEMBER 2025. The four labour Codes were brought into force on 21 November 2025, repealing the 29 central labour statutes this clause previously cited. CoW s.2(y) is the change that matters commercially: where allowances excluded from 'wages' exceed one-half of total remuneration, the excess is added back into wages, raising the PF, gratuity and bonus base. Most Indian CTC structures are built the other way round. The advocate should decide whether this clause should state the 50 per cent floor expressly so the employer cannot structure around it.
